title: ロボット設計演習Ⅰ
subtitle: Engineering Exercise for Robotics I
teachers:
FUJIKI Nobuaki
授業科目の学習・教育目標
educationalGoal:
(1) Learn mechanical design skills by designing a microcomputer car in a team environment.
(2) Practice mechanical drawing skills while designing the microcomputer car.
(3) Apply knowledge of mechanical design and machining to an actual robotic system.
advice:
This is a practical course in designing a robotic microcomputer car. We will cover the following topics:

1. Design of a steerage mechanism
2. Design of the structural frame
3. Machining and assembly of parts

Students are required to actively participate in class.
Students are expected to work together on a team to complete tasks in class.
Students are expected to machine some car parts after school hours.
books:
Textbooks:New JIS mechanical drawing(5th edition),Moritika Publishing(in Japanese)
Reference books:None
Reserved books:None
requiredKnowledge:
Completion of Engineering Mechanics I and II, Mechanics of Materials, and Mechanical Drawing I and II.
Sufficient skill in plate machining, drill press machining, milling machining, and (lathe) turning.
Students are required to not only have enough skills but also acquire a YUMEKOBO license (Sheet metal working, Drilling Machine, Lathes, and Milling Machine).

activityGoals.body: Understand and explain the major points of the design.
Understand the design process and how to design a microcomputer car.
Make detailed technical drawings compliant with JIS requirements with a computer-aided design system.
Create an assembly drawing and part drawings based on the machining that will be used for manufacturing.

              (1) Learn mechanical design skills by designing a microcomputer car in a team environment.
(2) Practice mechanical drawing skills while designing the microcomputer car.
(3) Apply knowledge of mechanical design and machining to an actual robotic system.

              授業の概要および学習上の助言

              This is a practical course in designing a robotic microcomputer car. We will cover the following topics:

1. Design of a steerage mechanism
2. Design of the structural frame
3. Machining and assembly of parts

Students are required to actively participate in class.
Students are expected to work together on a team to complete tasks in class.
Students are expected to machine some car parts after school hours.

Sufficient skill in plate machining, drill press machining, milling machining, and (lathe) turning.
Students are required to not only have enough skills but also acquire a YUMEKOBO license (Sheet metal working, Drilling Machine, Lathes, and Milling Machine).
